incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: canary-service-prod - error-rate spike above threshold (5xx 6.8% over 5m) · paging oncall @priya · runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/canary-failure
Maya: acked. I'm at my keyboard, hopping in.
Priya (oncall): I'm seeing increased 503s on canary slot a/b, CPU on canary nodes at 95% and OOM kills on one pod. Investigating logs now.
Priya (oncall): /svc/canary-service-prod namespace shows rollout v3.2.1 at 10% traffic.
Jason: that's my rollout. Enabled new-batcher feature flag (10% canary) at 11:22UTC. No infra changes.
Anika: any change in model weights or quantization?
Jason: no, model pinned. Only batching changes and kv-cache tweak.
Leo: logs show repeated "KVCache allocate failed: out of memory" from runtime-thread-3 on canary-2. Also a warning in router: "incompatible-kv-shard-size".
Maya: sounds like the new batching touched KV sizing. Can we flip the feature flag off as kill-switch?
Jason: yes please. I can flip but prefer ops to do it if automated rollback didn't fire.
Priya (oncall): trying the console toggle now. If anyone needs, runbook says: POST /api/v1/flags/new-batcher -> false
deploy-bot: Received flag toggle request from Priya. Executing toggle...
deploy-bot: Flag "new-batcher" -> disabled for canary (10%) by Priya at 11:37UTC :gear:
Priya (oncall): flag off. Looking for immediate effect on errors.
Sarah (support): I'm updating the support ticket queue: notifying EU customers of elevated errors in the last 20m. No direct P1 customer reports yet.
Priya (oncall): error-rate dropping from 6.8% -> 3.1% in 2m. But still above baseline. CPU still at ~88% on canary nodes.
Anika: automated rollback didn't trigger? why?
Leo: checked rollout-controller logs: "no rollback: metric name not found: latency.p50". The SLO name in controller config is "latency_p50" but metrics shipped as "latency.p50" after the batching change. Controller never matched threshold -> never triggered.
Maya: ugh. So manual rollback required. Can we cut traffic off the canary and restore previous release?
Jason: I'm ready to rollback to v3.2.0. Steps per runbook: scale canary down, repoint svc, redeploy previous revision.
Priya (oncall): doing manual rollback now. Commands I'm running:```bash
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/canary-service --to-revision=3
kubectl -n prod scale deployment/canary-service --replicas=2
# wait for pods ready
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/canary-service
```
Priya (oncall): rollback started. Notifying infra if anything unstable pops.
deploy-bot: Rollback command accepted by cluster. Starting rollout undo -> revision 3.
Priya (oncall): once pods ready will shift 10% traffic back to stable by updating route policy. Doing that after health checks.
Jason: once rollback completes I'll disable the canary route and run smoke tests.
Maya: smoke tests to run (from runbook):
- curl -sS https://canary.example/health | jq .status -> should be "ok"
- run end-to-end prompt through /v1/generate for a handful of seeds (seed set: fast-smoke-01)
- check kv-cache mem stats: `redis-cli -h kvcache-canary info memory`

Priya (oncall): rollback finished, new pods are Ready. Running smoke now.
Priya (oncall): health endpoint OK, sample generate responded, redis mem stable. Error rate down to 0.6% and CPU normalized to 48% on nodes.
Sarah (support): updating ticket: incident mitigated, customers informed, monitoring for 30m.
Anika: great. For postmortem: root cause likely batching code changed metric names + cache sizing regressed memory usage -> automated rollback failed and canary experienced OOMs.
Jason: assigning postmortem owners: me (release owner) + Anika (runtime) + Leo (metrics) · ETA drafts in 48h.
Maya: can someone file a runbook update: ensure rollout-controller supports metric aliasing or strict validation and add a test that validates metric name mapping during preflight?
Leo: will open PR for controller to accept both formats and add unit test.
Priya (oncall): monitoring will hold elevated alerting for 1h. I'll hand off to next oncall at 12:40UTC. @Maya please take next-step signoff.
Maya: taking handoff. Thanks everyone. Closing incident after monitoring window if stable. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: canary-service-prod - primary symptoms resolved, last update by Maya at 12:12UTC.
Maya: filing follow-up ticket and linking to this thread: https://redwood/boards/INC-4892
Jason: thanks team, will also disable the canary config for the next release until metric names verified.
Sarah (support): sending proactive email to impacted customers with summary and remediation steps.
Maya: good work. Postmortem owners assigned, action items tracked. Will update when postmortem draft ready. :memo:
